sets.topic: patay: ambiguity, uncertainty and source
sets.decisive_difference: Bare wording lacks a referent; murag adds uncertainty and giingon nila adds hearsay. Identified present human nonresponse or a current human death claim supports urgent verification, not confirmation.

sets.topic: patay: person versus engine

additional_illustrations.reason: Engine failure alone says nothing about injuries or remaining road hazards.

sets.decisive_difference: An explicitly stopped engine with everyone unhurt and safe supports minor. A current claim about a driver supports critical plus reported_unverified. The shared word is not the label.

sets.topic: patay: negation does not erase unconsciousness
sets.decisive_difference: Negating death while affirming unconsciousness remains urgent. Reporting a driver alive with unknown injuries does not prove minor.

sets.topic: dugo: amount, body site and missing context

additional_illustrations.reason: The amount is described but source and affected person are missing.
Possible severe bleeding warrants urgent clarification; subject and literal meaning remain unspecified.

sets.decisive_difference: A bare blood word is insufficient; a hand with small bleeding is a concrete injury; very heavy bleeding from a leg supports critical.

sets.topic: dugo: stopped bleeding versus ongoing heavy loss

additional_illustrations.reason: Stopped blood alone does not establish source, prior severity or current condition.

sets.decisive_difference: Stopped bleeding does not undo the hand injury. Continuous pouring blood supports greater urgency.

sets.topic: motubag: digital reply versus physical response

additional_illustrations.reason: Under a description-only contract the mode of nonresponse is unresolved; if a human is explicitly observed not responding, critical may be supported.

sets.decisive_difference: An unanswered message is not physical unresponsiveness. The observed bodily nonresponse in the longer fragment is informative despite short length.

sets.topic: naipit: unspecified subject, released finger, trapped occupant

additional_illustrations.reason: A localized finger injury is provisionally serious absent a supported life threat; not proof that circulation is safe.
Without an explicit human referent this could mean a person or object; urgently clarify rather than invent the subject.

sets.decisive_difference: Identify what is trapped and whether it is released. A released painful finger differs from a person unable to escape a vehicle.

sets.topic: sunog: extinguished safe scene versus occupied vehicle fire
sets.decisive_difference: A resolved fire with everyone unhurt and the scene safe differs from a person inside a currently burning car.

sets.topic: sunog: current versus historical
sets.decisive_difference: A current trapped occupant faces danger; a past fire with unknown current condition requires clarification.

sets.topic: conscious: concrete injury versus breathing distress
sets.decisive_difference: Being conscious does not determine severity. A painful knee and normal breathing differ from gasping with inability to speak.

sets.topic: conscious: question versus assertion
sets.decisive_difference: Asking whether someone is awake is uncertainty; directly describing an unconscious driver supports urgency.

sets.topic: conscious: conflict versus clear temporal change

additional_illustrations.reason: A chronological deterioration is coherent, not a contradiction.

sets.decisive_difference: Unresolved simultaneous contradictory reports differ from a clear current observation.

sets.topic: walking: no injury, painful injury, major bleeding
sets.decisive_difference: Walking can coexist with no injury, a knee injury or heavy bleeding. The condition and hazard evidence decide.

sets.topic: bali: human limb versus broken property
sets.decisive_difference: Bali applied to the reporter's foot or leg is a claimed injury; applied to a mirror with everyone safe is property damage.

sets.topic: bali: known arm injury versus unidentified object
sets.decisive_difference: A body part and possessor support a concrete injury; something broken without a visible referent is insufficient.

sets.topic: dili kalihok: localized arm, crushed chest, immobile car
sets.decisive_difference: The same inability-to-move idea describes different subjects and mechanisms; chest compression is an urgent hazard.

sets.topic: breathing: absence, impairment and uncertainty
sets.decisive_difference: Not breathing, gasping and uncertain breathing are distinct meanings; uncertainty must not be silently converted into normal breathing.

sets.topic: breathing: subject attribution

additional_illustrations.reason: Normal breathing in one person does not describe the unconscious passenger.

sets.decisive_difference: A well passenger cannot cancel a different person's absent breathing. Keep each condition attached to the right person.

sets.topic: crash: event-only versus explicit no injury and safety
sets.decisive_difference: Crash describes an event, not its severity. No injury plus safety supports minor; unknown condition requires review.

sets.topic: gasgas: object versus body versus absent subject

additional_illustrations.reason: The scratched subject and remaining danger are unspecified.

sets.decisive_difference: A vehicle scratch with explicit safety differs from a skin cut; lang does not erase injury.

sets.topic: cannot stand: impaired leg versus unsupported general request
sets.decisive_difference: A painful ankle or leg with impaired standing is an actual symptom; help alone offers no injury detail.

sets.topic: head injury: awake versus unresponsive
sets.decisive_difference: Wakefulness does not make a head cut minor; reported unresponsiveness establishes a separate urgent concern.

sets.topic: drowning: actual entrapment versus quoted scenario

additional_illustrations.text: For drill: passenger trapped underwater, no real crash.
additional_illustrations.reason: Explicit hypothetical context is out of scope for live severity classification.
A bare topic word lacks event, person and current-status context; urgently clarify.

sets.decisive_difference: A present trapped submerged passenger differs from an educational question.

sets.topic: fatality: present human claim versus undated forward
sets.decisive_difference: Current scene-linked hearsay can justify urgent verification without proving death. An undated or possibly old post does not establish present urgency.

sets.topic: injury: vague claim versus concrete wound
sets.decisive_difference: An unspecified hurt person needs clarification to locate urgency; a described hand wound or cut provides actionable injury evidence.

sets.topic: normal breathing: not equivalent to responsiveness

additional_illustrations.reason: Explicit unconsciousness remains urgent even with breathing reported.

sets.decisive_difference: Normal breathing does not establish that a person is responsive.
